reconcile.connective: Commentators harmonize the double listing as a sequence: the towns were Judah's first allotment, then ceded to Dan when Dan's territory was carved from Judah.

discrepancy.connective: W. F. Albright argued the Judah town-list is a separate administrative document of a different date from the tribal-boundary framework, so towns like Eshtaol and Zorah stand assigned to both Judah and Dan because the lists never represented one coherent distribution.

skeptic.name: W. F. Albright
skeptic.work: The Administrative Divisions of Israel and Judah, JPOS 5
skeptic.attribution: W. F. Albright (d. 1971), "The Administrative Divisions of Israel and Judah," Journal of the Palestine Oriental Society 5 (1925)

excerpts.excerpt_text: These places though first given to Judah, afterwards fell to the lot of Dan, Jos 19:41.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the Eshtaol/Zorah double-assignment: states the towns were Judah's first, then passed to Dan — the core harmonizing move keyed to both cited passages.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), on Joshua 15:33 and 19:41
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, explaining that Eshtaol and Zorah were first given to Judah and afterwards fell to the lot of Dan; chosen as the row-surfaced harmonizer keyed to this passage because Haley's specific coverage of this overlap could not be confirmed.

link.note: No allowlisted-domain page addresses the specific Eshtaol/Zorah Judah-vs-Dan double-assignment; link omitted rather than cite an off-topic page.
